vertical.caption: shopping bag
vertical.edit: The soft orange bag becomes a big paper shopping bag with two handles, full of the same bread, apples and lettuce; the hand still drops the water bottle in.

vertical.caption: tea bag
vertical.edit: The big bag is gone: the same hand dips a giant tea bag on a string into a huge steaming mug on the picnic blanket; the bread and apples lie beside the mug.

horizontal.caption: to drop a bag
horizontal.edit: The bag is falling, tipped on its side in mid-air just above the blanket, apples bouncing out and the bread sliding out; the man's open hands above, the bottle still in one of them.

question: What is the man doing?
answerWhy: Matches the clip: he puts apples, bread, a lettuce and a water bottle into the bag on the picnic blanket. Present continuous for the ongoing action, "pack a bag with food" is a correct collocation, level A words only.
notes: Close-up still, so "to carry a bag" (needs the full body) and "sleeping bag" (would replace the whole picnic) were dropped; 4 images total. No nouns row: the nouns (bread, apples, shirt) appear inside the other phrases only indirectly; the 4 non-carousel rows come from taps and the answer.
